summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, CAD s/p CABG, atrial fibrillation, alcoholism, and chronic anemia was admitted for acute dyspnea and fever following alcohol ingestion. Initial evaluation revealed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, likely due to missed diltiazem, which resolved with medication. Workup ruled out acute coronary syndrome, but a repeat chest X-ray showed left lower lobe opacity consistent with aspiration pneumonia, prompting IV antibiotics. He also had acute kidney injury and metabolic acidosis, both attributed to dehydration and alcohol use, which improved with IV fluids. Anemia and thrombocytopenia were stable for his baseline and thought to be multifactorial from chronic disease and alcohol. He completed a course of IV antibiotics, transitioned to oral levofloxacin, and was started on a 5-day prednisone taper for COPD exacerbation. He improved clinically, became afebrile, and was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation and completion of treatment.
